families.theme: Wild teakettle logging-camp folklore and misleading opposite snowshoe tracks: a warm spout-mouthed creature grows a pressure chest and oversized feet pointing in opposite directions.

evolution_design.regional_evidence: A North Shore tall tale describes a hissing spout-mouth creature whose odd feet leave snowshoe tracks pointing in opposite directions.
evolution_design.original_invention: Kettle-like chest, pressure anatomy and the precise three-stage shapes below are original design inventions, not a claimed historical illustration.

body_growth.body: Small squat warm-bodied sprite; short spout muzzle, lid-like brow, two little oval feet with opposite toe directions. Compact alert face.
body_growth.silhouette: Low teardrop chest, one projecting muzzle, two deliberately mismatched foot tips; no separate held kettle.

body_growth.body: Chest expands into a rounded pressure body, muzzle lengthens, and the two feet broaden into opposed snowshoe paddles. One short steam curl marks the mouth.
body_growth.silhouette: Round chest above two long low ovals pointing away from one another; the feet become the unmistakable family signature.

body_growth.body: Very low horizontal pressure beast: long continuous arched spine, longer forward spout head, two folded short forearms beneath its chest, and enormous opposed snowshoe feet at opposite ends. Three vent slits remain on the chest.
body_growth.silhouette: Long low arch nearly twice as wide as tall, broad foot ovals at the two ends with one wide dark opening each; crouched pivoting anatomy changes the upright middle-stage silhouette.

families.silhouette_concept: Opposed snowshoe feet grow from a tiny visual joke into a strong wide base; body volume and pressure anatomy increase at each stage. Black anchors around solid anatomy; steam stays a small controlled effect.
families.habitat: Cutover second-growth woods above the North Shore, with snowy trail margins in winter.

families.theme: Ancient underwater pillow-lava inflation and breakout growth, embodied as a quenched-crust creature that develops a long molten spine.

evolution_design.regional_evidence: NPS documents ancient pillow structures in Voyageurs greenstone, including an islet near Steamboat Island north of Cranberry Bay. Basalt pillows form underwater; this is ancient geology, not an active Minnesota volcano.
evolution_design.original_invention: A dormant pillow-body creature reawakens internal heat; the living molten spine and evolutionary anatomy are fiction. No real exposure is claimed at a map coordinate.

body_growth.body: One low inflated lobe with a short molten mouth seam and four nubby crust fins; its back looks swollen rather than angular.
body_growth.silhouette: One squat bean with a forward seam-mouth and low fins.

body_growth.silhouette: Three overlapping round volumes with a distinct blunt head and raised belly gap.

body_growth.body: A long low wyrm develops a solid molten spine between separated inflated shell lobes. Four broad crust fins brace it, while two blunt basalt crown prongs frame the face.
body_growth.silhouette: Long segmented arch, four strong side fins and a forked blunt crown; no wings or thin serpent tail.

families.theme: Stromatolite fossil colonies become a living archive of many tiny vanished lives; successive mound growth changes a solitary dome into a cooperative stone apparition.

evolution_design.original_invention: Ghost inhabitants, shared faces and free-standing archive anatomy are original fantasy. The fossil organisms themselves were microscopic colonies, not the proposed monster shapes.

families.theme: Thermal lake-ice cracking and dry-winter static combine into a split-plate clapper creature that stores charge between opposing ice slabs.

evolution_design.regional_evidence: Minnesota DNR explains temperature-driven ice contraction, cracks and expansion. NWS describes static charge in dry winter air. These are two real inspirations, not evidence that ordinary ice cracks generate lightning.
evolution_design.original_invention: A body that transfers winter static through its ice-plate arms is fictional. The evolutionary mechanism is widening separated slabs, not increasingly dense crack decoration.

body_growth.body: A broad asymmetric three-lobed lichen mantle folds over one stout rock anchor-foot. One large eye peers from the sheltered fold; two broad curled mantle tips frame the face, and the lower dark underside remains one simple solid shape.
body_growth.silhouette: Low three-lobed scalloped canopy around a single high stone foot and one eye; broad folded flaps rather than stippled lichen texture or a mushroom cap.
